observation_summary: The method NumberUtils.createNumber throws a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of a NumberFormatException when processing invalid numeric strings containing both 'e' and 'E' (e.g., '1eE').
reasoning_summary: The fix involves adding explicit checks (if-statements) to validate the position of the exponent indicator ('expPos') relative to the string length before performing substring operations. Since the root cause is a missing validation check that leads to an out-of-bounds access, this is a classic 'Checking' defect.
evidence_used: The fix adds 'if (expPos > str.length())' checks to validate input before calling substring.
The bug report states the code throws a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of a NumberFormatException.
The stack trace confirms the exception occurs during a substring operation in NumberUtils.createNumber.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The fix is not changing the computational logic of parsing, but rather adding a guard condition to prevent invalid state/input from reaching the substring method.
